events.title: 7:30 PM Cassiof and Iva Mai Concert
events.description: Cassiof, a Brussels band performing French pop-rap chanson. A concert to sweep us all away.

events.title: Back-to-School Party — Season 5
events.description: A big celebration to kick off this 5th season, on the street and inside the House, featuring concerts, DJ sets, performances, a creator marketplace and lots of surprises! It's free with no reservation needed—just drop by, we'd love to have you!

events.title: Unruly Roses
events.description: The hollyhock (alcea rosea) is a perennial plant whose name is thought to derive from 'Rose from Overseas.' All its parts are edible and its medicinal properties have been recognized since antiquity. Their presence in Brussels creates a striking contrast: their wild, untamed nature, their large colorful flowers disturb the urban order and we […]

events.title: Reading bell hooks, Living Culture: Arts, Representations and Spaces of Belonging and Resistance
events.description: To mark the release of Non silenciées: Affirm, Rebel, Live, Maison poème and The Gallery Wetsi present a public discussion on the contemporary relevance of bell hooks' thinking. Afrofeminist sociologist and essayist Fania Noël will dialogue with art historian and curator Anne Wetsi Mpoma about two works by bell […]

events.title: 5-7pm Organic Produce Baskets from Nadir Farm
events.description: Fresh vegetable baskets all year round! Each year, households commit to picking up a weekly vegetable basket and building local food sovereignty. This is our CSA, our Community Supported Agriculture. The basket contents are a delightful mix of classic vegetables and exciting new flavors that we cultivate without fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, or fossil fuel-powered tools—just lots of love.

events.title: Poetry, No Need to Fear! — CotCotCot Celebrates 15 Years
events.description: On September 9th, CotCotCot editions takes over Maison poème to showcase the poetic side of their catalog through 5 readings, accompanied by a musical composition by Raphaël Decoster, musician from the band Turfu and illustrator of the album All My Pebbles. For this special evening, designed for their 15th anniversary, we […]

events.title: 6pm Lecture Performance: Be Passive and Shut Up! Or How Classist Policies Keep Us From Real Democracy
events.description: Since 2010, Donatienne has been helping households make the most of energy-efficient and socially-minded housing to meet energy savings and comfort goals. It's complicated, right?! Really, she's above all a social worker! And that's what she's standing up for today.

events.title: Storm Beasts
events.description: Storm Beasts, it's this woman who speaks, raps, twerks. You won't understand right away what she wants and that's just fine. There's her grandmother too, her daughter somewhere and the stage manager. And then there's abortion, literal and figurative. Attempts and failures. Laughter or tears. Raw […]

events.title: 6pm Exploration of 'Rule of Law': Bourgeois Order by Elsa Marcel
events.description: Rule of Law: Bourgeois Order. In the face of authoritarian governments, police violence, and colonial reaction...

events.title: "We Are Not Condemned to Cowardice"
events.description: A reading circle around Catherine Dorion's book, connected to the philosophy evening "Crossing the Fascist Storm" happening the same night. These new regular gatherings are designed as warm moments where people can share their thoughts, learn from others, and discuss the book in connection with the venue's programming.

events.title: Crossing the Fascist Storm
events.description: As part of the Philosophy Evenings at Maison poème, a meeting with Québécois author and theater artist Catherine Dorion, discussing her book The Courage and the Joy, subtitled "Crossing the Fascist Storm Without Losing Your Way". The discussion will be moderated by independent journalist Manon Legrand (Vie Féminine, Axelle, Alter Echos...).

events.title: 5-7pm organic produce boxes from Nadir Farm
events.description: Fresh vegetable boxes all year round! Every year, households commit to picking up a weekly vegetable box and building local food sovereignty. It's our CSA—our Community Supported Agriculture initiative. The box contents are a delightful blend of classic vegetables and exciting new flavors, which we grow without synthetic fertilizers, pesticides, herbicides, or fossil fuel-powered tools, but with plenty of love.

events.title: Women's Kiaï
events.description: In an improvised dojo at the heart of the Women's House in Schaerbeek, Brussels, women gather to experience a unique space at the intersection of body and voice. Through exercises inspired by karate and theater led by Valérie Gimenez, they explore their limits, fears, and breath.

events.title: 7:30pm Jun Sandson Concert
events.description: Jun Sandson is a multidisciplinary indie pop artist, singer-songwriter, and performer. A quirky clown spinning through sounds somewhere between raw blues, free folk, and experimental music. A delightfully odd character, half-deaf, singing melancholic "melocoton" songs to lift people's spirits again!

events.title: My Little Big Chop
events.description: As a DEI (Diversity, Equity and Inclusion) officer at a startup, Emma faces a string of romantic and hair-related mishaps. Usually she keeps a low profile, but her wig is irritating and mirrors have become unbearable. Her YouTube aunties warned her: there's no going back. She's turning 30 tomorrow and ready to make her mark [...]

events.title: 11am Literary Encounter with Romain Lemire and Thomas Prédour
events.description: Romain Lemire received the Goncourt Prize for First Novel for "Clément," a powerful account of the incest he and his brothers endured for years. He will receive the title of Doctor Honoris Causa from ULB on September 18th. Thomas Prédour created the show "It Was Just a Game," from which he developed a self-published book that also addresses the theme of incest. They will discuss together the reasons that led them to write on this subject and will read passages...

events.title: 6pm Walking Tour through "Eaters—Stories of Those Who Devour, Savor, or Fast Excessively" by Lauren Malka
events.description: In Eaters, journalist and podcaster Lauren Malka investigates women's relationship with food and their bodies. Tracing through history, literature, and culture...

Stone Garden is an attempt to make our differences resonate through a poetic gesture in the street. An invitation to listen to each other, to connect [...]

events.title: From O to A
events.description: An evening of duo concerts. Featuring an unconventional concert by Karin Clercq and Pascal Charpentier, with an intimate version of Raphaële Germser's repertoire as opener!

events.title: Offline

events.title: Two Minute Chance
events.description: Presents: "Two Minute Chance" - A hilarious performance featuring catchy sing-alongs delivered in authentic Brussels dialect. These are the key ingredients of this singing duo. Daniël Robbrecht and Peter Decabooter bring Brussels humor back to life with synthesizer, guitar, and their distinctive two-part harmonies. Expect a mix of imaginative Brussels renditions of well-known songs alongside their original repertoire, all performed in the 'Vloms' Brussels style. "Two Minute Chance" delivers atmosphere, conviviality, and fun. Sunday, September 27, 2026 at Het Goudblommeke in Papier at 3 PM.

events.title: The Pigeon and the Lazarus Bird
events.description: An ordinary wildlife documentary about a pigeon takes a dramatic turn when a fire threatens its existence. While fleeing, it comes face-to-face with a mysterious bird, supposedly extinct for millennia. But their curious encounter may have been no accident at all.

events.description: A polyphonic concert to tell the story of loss, to say or resay goodbye, to shed tears or share knowing smiles with those who have passed. These polyphonic songs are created based on intimate experiences and life encounters. We sing in three-part harmony, a cappella, in French and English [...]

events.title: Letters on Enthusiasm — Launch Evening
events.description: With everything collapsing around us, how can we stay enthusiastic? How do we move forward? Is it possible to sustain enthusiasm? To lose it entirely? Or perhaps to embrace collective enthusiasm together? That's the idea behind this book: inviting 26 women writers to share their relationship with enthusiasm through letters [...]

events.title: Sylvie Savon
events.description: Who is Sylvie Savon? She's the kind of woman who messes everything up, but with grace. Arrogant, free, lost and funny in spite of herself, she's our heroine—a real-life hero of resourcefulness and uncertain tomorrows. No career, no family, no pension plan—just an apartment plan [...]

events.title: Prophetic Dance on the Strange Island
events.description: In the heart of a white forest, performance artist Geneviève Matthieu undergoes metamorphoses amid the cries and howls of the night. Through poetry, physical training, music and song, she invokes a strange island where landmarks waver and where the living, memories and invisible presences coexist in a single breath. [...]

events.title: Bands of Hysterics
events.description: Screening of the film Bands of Hysterics, directed by Kita Bauchet. Bands of Hysterics tells the little-known history of women's emancipation movements in the 1970s in Belgium. From the bold actions of Dolle Mina in Flanders, to the support of female workers by Marie Mineur in Wallonia, to the International Tribunal on Crimes Against Women that brought together in Brussels [...]

events.title: ERASMUS PLEADS FOR PEACE
events.description: a tale by Frank Jacobs and Chris Reunes. What would peace tell us if she were a woman of flesh and blood? How would she convince us to stop war and violence? Erasmus asked himself this question back in 1517 because the world was on fire then too. He wrote THE LAMENTATION OF PEACE, a text that has remained meaningful, especially today. Frank JACOBS and Chris REUNES present to you THE LAMENTATION OF PEACE, with text excerpts, commentary and image projection. They also bring satirical dialogues in which Erasmus dismisses all violence as crime with razor-sharp mockery. An hour of laughter.
